fieldMarks: Male: bold white 'spectacles' around the eye on a green head, black chest and underparts, white back
Female: mottled brown with a hint of the male's face pattern
Large round eye patch of different colour and texture is present in downy chicks and all plumages
Common and King eiders have a bill frontal process reaching near the eye; the spectacled eider does not, and its forehead feathering runs far forward to just behind the nostril
Common eider is distinctly larger and King eider slightly larger than spectacled eider
behavior: Small compact flocks; huge dense flocks in openings in sea ice in winter
Dives longer than most diving ducks; eats mollusks and crustaceans at sea
Summer tundra diet includes aquatic insects, sedges, grasses and berries
Migrates offshore over the Bering, Chukchi and Beaufort seas
habitat: Breeds in wet coastal tundra with shallow ponds; otherwise at sea, often among pack ice.
range: Breeds in Arctic Alaska (Beaufort Sea west to Norton Sound and the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta) and eastern Russia; non-breeding in the Bering and Chukchi seas.

lookalikes.name: Common eider
